*Moving* is the act of a *Game Object* moving between two *Locations* on *The Board.*
  *See rule 445. Movement for more information on movement.*
modifiedPrev.420.2.a: Players may only move *Game Objects* when instructed to do so by Game Effects or costs.
modifiedPrev.420.3: The *Standard Move* inherent to *Units* is a *Discretionary Action.*
modifiedPrev.421.1: *Hiding* a card is the act of placing a card facedown at a *Battlefield* you control.
modifiedPrev.421.2.a:
The *Hidden* keyword allows a player to pay a cost to *Hide* a card any time they have a *Hidden* card in their hand or Champion Zone and meet the prerequisites.
  *See rule 811. Hidden for more information.*
modifiedPrev.421.3:
Cards that are facedown at *Battlefields* have their gameplay properties and permissions defined by the effect that put them there.
  *Example:* Cards that players *Hide* with the *Hidden* keyword can be *Played* for [0] on any subsequent turn as a property of the *Hidden* keyword.
modifiedPrev.422.1: *Discarding* a card is moving it from a player's hand directly into their trash without activating or executing its normal rules text.
modifiedPrev.422.2.a: A player must *Discard* cards when instructed to do so by game effects or costs.
modifiedPrev.422.3:
When *Discarding* is listed as a *Cost*, then the Action must be able to be completed for the cost to be paid.
  *Example:* A card has the ability "Discard 2: Deal 2 damage to a unit at a battlefield." To activate the ability, the card's controller must have at least 2 cards in hand and must be able to discard them.
modifiedPrev.422.4:
When *Discarding* is part of an effect, then a player must *Discard* as many cards as possible from their hand. If instructed to discard more cards than they have in their hand, further discard instructions are ignored.
  *Example:* Undercover Agent has the ability "[Deathknell][>] Discard 2, then draw 2. (When I die, get the effect.)" If Undercover Agent's controller has 2 or more cards in hand, they must discard 2. If they have 1 card in hand, they discard 1, and the rest of the discard instruction is ignored. If they have no cards in hand, the entire discard instruction is ignored. Regardless of how many cards they discard, they then draw 2.
modifiedPrev.423.1: *Stunning* is the act of selecting one or more *Units* on *the Board* and rendering them *Stunned.*
modifiedPrev.423.1.a: *Stunned* is a binary state. A *Unit* is *Stunned* or it isn't.
modifiedPrev.423.1.b:
A *Stunned Unit* does not contribute its might to damage in the combat damage step.
  *See rule 465. The Combat Damage Step for more information.*
modifiedPrev.423.2.a: Players may only *Stun Units* when directed to by *Game Effects.*
modifiedPrev.424.1: *Revealing* is the act of presenting a card to *all players* from a zone that one or more players do not have access to the information of.
modifiedPrev.424.1.a: *Revealed* is a temporary state and is not a zone.
modifiedPrev.424.1.a.1: Other cards, including the card being revealed, can reference the act of *being Revealed.*
modifiedPrev.424.1.a.2:
Cards remain in the zone they are being *Revealed* from.
  *Example:* If a card is being *Revealed* from the top of a player's *Main Deck*, it is still the top card of that player's *Main Deck.*
modifiedPrev.424.1.b: Unless otherwise described, *Revealed* cards do nothing else beyond become temporarily known information to *all players.*
modifiedPrev.424.2.a: Players may only *Reveal* cards from *Private* or *Secret* zones when instructed to do so by *Game Effects.*
modifiedPrev.425.1: *Countering* is the act of negating the execution, activation, or otherwise playing of a card or ability by a player.
modifiedPrev.425.1.a: A card or ability that is *Countered* does nothing and is cleared from the chain.
modifiedPrev.425.1.a.1: Cards that are cleared from the chain in this way are placed in the trash.
modifiedPrev.425.1.b: A card that is *Countered* is not considered to have been played for abilities that trigger on cards being played.
modifiedPrev.425.2.a: Players may only *Counter* cards and abilities when directed to by *Game Effects.*
modifiedPrev.425.3: This action is formatted as "*Counter* [a card or ability on the chain]."
modifiedPrev.426.1:
*Buffing* is the action of placing a *Buff* counter on a *Unit*.
  *See rule 701. Buffs for more information.*
modifiedPrev.426.1.b: To *Buff* a unit, place a *Buff Counter* on it if it does not have one already
modifiedPrev.426.1.c:
Units with *Buff Counters* can still be chosen for actions that *Buff* units, but will *not* be *Buffed* as part of the execution.
  *Example:* A spell reads "Buff a unit. Then, if it was buffed this way, draw a card." It will place a buff counter on a unit that has no buff counter, and then its controller will draw a card. However, if the player chooses a unit with a buff counter on it already, then the card will not be drawn.
  *Example:* A unit reads “When you buff me, ready me.” If that unit is chosen for a game effect that would buff it and it is already buffed, its ability will not trigger.
modifiedPrev.426.2.a: Players may only *Buff* units when *Game Effects* direct them to do so.
modifiedPrev.426.3: This action is formatted as "*Buff* [one or more units]." *e.g.,* "Buff a unit." *e.g.,* "Buff a friendly unit." *e.g.,* "Buff two friendly units at the same battlefield."
modifiedPrev.427.1:
*Banishing* is the action of placing a card from any other zone into *Banishment.*
  *See 108.6. Banishment for more information.*
modifiedPrev.427.2: When a card is *Banished* it is placed directly into the *Banishment* zone from its origin.
modifiedPrev.427.2.a: Banish is not a subset of *Kill.*
modifiedPrev.427.3: Cards and effects can refer to cards that were banished *by the same object.*
modifiedPrev.428.1: *Killing* is the action of a *Permanent* going to the trash from the board.
modifiedPrev.428.2: When a *permanent* is *killed* it is placed directly in the trash from its place of origin.
modifiedPrev.428.2.a: It is only considered *Killed* if its origin was any zone on the board.
modifiedPrev.428.2.b: This is not a subset of *Move.*
modifiedPrev.428.3.a: Players may only *Kill* units when *Game Effects* direct them to do so.
modifiedPrev.428.4: *Killing* can also be the result of resolving a *Cleanup.*
modifiedPrev.428.5: *Killing* can be attributed to one or more *Game Objects.*
modifiedPrev.429.1: *Adding* is the action of putting resources into a player's *Rune Pool.*
modifiedPrev.429.2: Triggered and activated abilities that *Add* resources resolve as soon as they are finalized.
modifiedPrev.429.2.a: *Priority* and *Focus* will not pass from *Add* abilities being finalized or resolving, and will resolve before any other outstanding items on the chain are finalized.
modifiedPrev.429.2.b: Spells that *Add* resources will linger on the chain as normal when they are finalized.
modifiedPrev.429.3:
Activated abilities that *Add* resources and have the *Reaction* tag can be activated at any time that spells or abilities require resources be paid.
  *Example:* A player can add Energy and Power through any means before initiating the process of playing a spell. After initiating that process, in the Pay Costs step, they may activate *Add Reactions* to add Energy or Power to pay costs.
  *Example:* A player moves two units to a battlefield where their opponent controls a Mageseeker Investigator. Although they have no window of priority, they may activate *Add Reactions* to pay for the applied cost from Mageseeker Investigator, and those abilities finalize and resolve immediately.
modifiedPrev.429.3.a: When an *Add* ability is activated in this way, it immediately finalizes and resolves, even during the resolution of spells and abilities.
modifiedPrev.429.5: This action is formatted as "Add [one or more resources]." *e.g.,* "Add [2]." means "Add 2 Energy." *e.g.,* "[E]: Add [Y]." means "Add 1 Power of the Order domain." *e.g.,* "Add [1][G]." means "Add 1 Energy and 1 Power of the Calm domain."
modifiedPrev.430.1: *Channeling* is the action of taking one or more *Runes* from the top of a player's *Rune Deck* and putting them on the board.
modifiedPrev.430.2:
The *Game Effect* that instructs a player to channel 1 or more runes may specify the conditions or circumstances under which those runes enter the board.
  *Example:* A spell reads "Channel 1 rune exhausted." As that spell resolves, its controller puts the top rune of their rune deck onto the board and that rune enters the board exhausted rather than ready.
modifiedPrev.430.2.a: By default, runes are channeled readied.
modifiedPrev.430.3: If there aren’t sufficient runes in the *Rune Deck,* channel as many as possible.
modifiedPrev.430.4.a: A player *Channels* two *Runes* during the *Channel Phase* on their turn.
modifiedPrev.430.5:
This action is formatted as "Channel X rune(s)," optionally followed by conditions or stipulations.
  *e.g.,* "Channel 1 rune." *e.g.,* "When you play me, channel 1 rune exhausted." *e.g.,* "Channel 2 runes exhausted. If you couldn't channel 2 runes this way, draw 1."
modifiedPrev.431.1: *Burning Out* is an action a player must perform if they attempt to move one or more cards from their *Main Deck* to any other zone in excess of the number of cards remaining in their *Main Deck:*
modifiedPrev.431.2: To *Burn Out*, a player does the following in sequence:
modifiedPrev.431.2.a: Performs as much of the prescribed action as possible.
modifiedPrev.431.3: A player's Main Deck may remain empty as they *Burn Out*, usually because their trash is also empty. When they attempt to perform the original action again, it will cause another *Burn Out*.
modifiedPrev.431.4.a: Players may only burn out when *Game Effects* direct them to do so.
modifiedPrev.431.5:
*Burning Out* is a *Replacement Effect.*
  *See rule 367. Replacement Effects for more information.*
modifiedPrev.432.1: *Doubling* is the act of *increasing* a numeric attribute by an amount equal to that attribute’s current value.
modifiedPrev.432.1.a:
This creates an effect that modulates that attribute by that specific amount for the duration specified by the *Game Effect* that instructed the player to perform this action.
  *Example: A unit with 3 base Might and Shield 2 is in combat as a Defender. Since Shield applies, its current Might is 5. A player chooses it as the target for Last Stand, a spell that reads in part “Double a friendly unit's Might this turn.” Its current Might is 5, so it gets +5 Might this turn, for a current Might of 10. After combat, Shield no longer applies, but the +5 Might from Last Stand does, so the unit’s Might is 8.*
modifiedPrev.432.2.a: Players may only Double when *Game Effects* direct them to do so.
modifiedPrev.433.1: *Swapping* is the act of increasing one numeric value and decreasing another numeric value on some number of *Game Objects* such that their values are reversed.
modifiedPrev.433.1.a: *Swapping* creates two different effects that apply to each attribute. One that *Increases* one value and one that *Decreases* the other. These effects last for the duration specified by the effect that instructed the *Swap.*
modifiedPrev.433.1.b: To accomplish this, determine the difference between these values and then apply an *Increase* for that amount to the lower value of the two attributes, and a *Decrease* of that amount to the higher value of the two attributes.
modifiedPrev.433.2.a: Players may only swap when *Game Effects* direct them to do so.
modifiedPrev.434.1:
*Attaching* is the act of linking two cards on the board together to combine their effects in some way. This causes one or more cards to become *Attached* and at least one card to become a *Top-Most Card.*
  *See rule 716. Attachment for more information.*
modifiedPrev.434.1.b: This is represented by physically laying the *Top-Most card* on top of the other or others such that all *Effect Texts* and *Might Bonuses* are showing, but nothing else from the card or cards *Attached.*
modifiedPrev.434.1.c: The *Top-Most card* has all *Effect Text* of all cards *Attached* to it appended to its *Rules Text.*
modifiedPrev.434.1.d: The *Top-Most Card* has its *Might* modulated by the *Might Bonus* of all cards *Attached* to it.
modifiedPrev.434.2.a: Players may only *Attach* cards when directed to by *Game Effects.*
modifiedPrev.435.1: *Detaching* is the act of unlinking two cards that are currently linked through the act of *Attaching*. This causes one to cease being *Attached*, and potentially causes the other to cease being a *Top-Most card.*
modifiedPrev.435.1.a: *Detaching* affects only cards that are currently *Attached* to another card.
modifiedPrev.435.1.a.1: Game effects that instruct a player to *Detach* a card that is currently not *Attached* to anything will do nothing.
modifiedPrev.435.1.b: When one or more cards become *Detached*, they cease to be in the *Attached* state.
modifiedPrev.435.1.b.1: To represent this, these cards should no longer be placed under the card they were previously placed under as *Top-Most Card.*
modifiedPrev.435.1.c: The card being *Detached* has its *Effect Text* become *Inactive* and its *Rules Text* cease being *Inactive.*
modifiedPrev.435.1.d: The *Top-Most Card* ceases to have the *Effect Text* of the card being *Detached* appended to its *Rules Text.*
modifiedPrev.435.1.e: The *Top-Most Card* ceases to have its *Might* modulated by the *Might Bonus* of the card being *Detached.*
modifiedPrev.435.2.a: *Players* may only *Detach* cards when directed to by *Game Effects.*
modifiedPrev.435.3: *Detaching* cards does not inherently choose, or specify a target. However, Game Effects that *Detach* cards may.
modifiedPrev.435.4: When a card *Detaches* from a *Top-Most Card*, its location is the same as the *Top-Most Card* from which it *Detached.*
modifiedPrev.435.4.a:
If the *Detached* card was a *Gear* and this causes it to become present at a *Battlefield*, it will be *Recalled* during the next *Cleanup.*
  *See rule 318. Cleanups for more information.*
modifiedPrev.436.1: *Predicting* a card is the act of looking at a single card from the top of the *Main Deck* and choosing whether or not to *Recycle* it.
modifiedPrev.436.1.a: When more than one card is *Predicted*, the *Predicting* player looks at that many cards and *Recycles* any number of them before putting the rest back on top of their *Main Deck* in any order.
modifiedPrev.436.2.a: *Players* may only *Predict* cards when instructed to do so by game effects.
modifiedPrev.436.3: This action, when instructed, is formatted as "Predict X."
modifiedPrev.436.4: If a player attempts to *Predict* more cards than are available in their *Main Deck*, they will *Predict* as many as possible instead.
modifiedPrev.436.4.a: The *Player* will not perform a *Burn Out* as a result of *Predicting* with too few cards in their deck.
modifiedPrev.437.1: *Preventing* damage is the act of reducing the *Damage* a set of game objects would take.
modifiedPrev.437.1.a: *Prevent* is an action that interacts with *Damage.*
modifiedPrev.437.2: When damage is *Prevented*, it is replaced with an event where it deals that much damage reduced by the Prevent Value tracked on the *Unit* specifically.
modifiedPrev.437.2.a: The damage being dealt as a result of *Preventing* can never be less than 0, but can be 0. This is equivalent to not dealing damage.
modifiedPrev.437.3: When damage is dealt this way, reduce the Prevent Value being tracked on the *Unit* affected by the *Prevent* action by the prevented amount.
modifiedPrev.437.3.a: If the Prevent Value is 0 or less, then *Prevent* is no longer being tracked on the *Unit* in question, and the effect expires.
modifiedPrev.437.4: Damage dealt to a *Unit* that has that all of that damage *Prevented* is not considered to have been dealt to it at all.
modifiedPrev.438.1: *Replacing* is the act of *Creating* a token in the place of another card or token without playing it while inheriting all effects or statuses of the game object it replaced.
modifiedPrev.438.1.a:
The replacing token is treated as the same *Game Object* as the card or token it replaced for the purposes of *Game Effects* that target or reference that game object.
  *Example:* A player with Green Father as their legend conquers Navori Fighting Pit. They choose to place the Green Father conquer effect on the chain after the Navori Fighting Pit conquer effect. When the Green Father trigger resolves, Navori Fighting Pit is replaced with Brush. Although the Navori Fighting Pit has been replaced, the “here” in its triggered ability still can have its information referenced, because the Brush inherited all statuses and conditions. The unit Navori Fighting Pit’s triggered ability has targeted will still be a legal target on resolution.
modifiedPrev.438.2.a: The player may *Replace* cards and tokens when instructed to do so by other game effects.
modifiedPrev.438.3: This action, when instructed, is formatted as "Replace [X] with [Y]."
modifiedPrev.438.3.a: The [X] is the target to be *Replaced.*
modifiedPrev.438.3.b: The [Y] is the object that will *Replace* the target.
modifiedPrev.438.5: The card or token that is *Replaced* is placed in Banishment.
modifiedPrev.438.5.a: While it resides in *Banishment,* it is considered to have been *Replaced* and not *Banished.*
modifiedPrev.438.6: If a token is *Replaced* it will stop existing once it begins its occupancy in *Banishment.*
modifiedPrev.438.6.a: This does not invalidate the token created, or the act of *Replacement.*
modifiedPrev.438.7: Tokens that have been *Created* through a *Replace* action can be instructed to be “Swapped back.” This may also appear as “replace [the token] with the [*Game Object*] it replaced.”
modifiedPrev.439.1: *Creating* is the act of producing a *Game Object* that previously did not exist in the game.
modifiedPrev.439.2: Effects that *Create* one or more *Game Objects* will direct where those *Game Objects* must go - the *Game Objects* are *Created* directly to the zones in question.
modifiedPrev.439.2.a: Prior to being *Created,* these *Game Objects* did not exist outside of the zone they were *Created* to. After being *Created*, they may change zones as appropriate for *Game Objects* of their type.
modifiedPrev.439.3: An effect that *Creates* a *Game Object* will specify the state and nature of the *Game Object* created.
modifiedPrev.439.3.a:
If the *Game Object* is a token, it will follow the normal rules for tokens.
  *See rule 179. Tokens for more information.*
modifiedPrev.439.4: Unless specified otherwise by the *Game Effect* that *Creates* a *Game Object*, any such *Game Object* is owned by the player who *Created* it. *Control* is established as usual for *Game Objects* of the appropriate type.
modifiedPrev.439.5: This action, when instructed, is usually formatted as "Create [X] at [Y]" or “Add [X] to [Y].”
modifiedPrev.439.6.a: Players may only *Create Game Objects* when directed to by *Game Effects.*
modifiedPrev.440.1: *Burning* is the act of moving cards from the top of a player’s *Main Deck* to their trash.
modifiedPrev.440.2: This action is formatted as "Burn X."
modifiedPrev.440.2.a: X is the number of cards to be *Burned.*
modifiedPrev.440.3.a: A player must *Burn* cards when instructed to do so by game effects or costs.
modifiedPrev.440.4:
When *Burning* is part of an effect, then a player must *Burn* as many cards as possible. If instructed to burn more cards than they have in their main deck, they burn that many cards, burn out and then burn the rest.
  *See rule 431. Burn Out for more information.*
modifiedPrev.441.1: *Empowering* is the act of rendering one or more *Game Objects Empowered.*
modifiedPrev.441.1.a: *Empowered* is a binary state. A *Game Object* is *Empowered* or it isn’t.
modifiedPrev.441.2: *“Empowered”* is a state for *Game Objects* on the board that other game effects and abilities can reference.
modifiedPrev.441.2.a: When a *Game Object* becomes *Empowered* as a result of the *Empower* game action, that is an event that can similarly be referenced by game effects and abilities.
modifiedPrev.441.3.a: Players may only *Empower Game Objects* when directed to by *Game Effects.*
modifiedPrev.442.1: *Disempowering* is the act of removing the *Empowered* status from one or more *Game Objects.*
modifiedPrev.442.1.a: *Disempowering* affects only cards that are currently *Empowered.*
modifiedPrev.442.2.a: Players may only *Disempower Game Objects* when directed to by *Game Effects.*
modifiedPrev.443.1: *Skipping* an event is the act of replacing that event with nothing.
modifiedPrev.443.1.a:
*Skip* is an action that interacts with events and procedures of the turn.
  Example: A card reads in part “Choose an enemy unit. Skip the next time that unit would move this turn.” This is a replacement effect that replaces the event of a unit moving with nothing.
  Example: A card reads in part “Skip your Draw phase.” This is a replacement effect that replaces a player’s Draw Phase with nothing.
  Example: A card reads in part “Choose a player. They skip their next point from conquering this turn.” This is a replacement effect that replaces the 1 point gained when conquering with nothing.
modifiedPrev.443.1.a.1:
An event is the singular moment that results from a Game Action being performed or from a Game Object changing state.
  See rule 367. Replacement Effects for more information.
modifiedPrev.443.1.b: *Skip* actions are usually formatted as “Skip [event or procedure of the turn].”
modifiedPrev.443.2: When an event or procedure of the turn is *Skipped,* it is replaced with nothing. Play proceeds accordingly.
modifiedPrev.443.2.a: Anything that triggers on the occurrence of the event or procedure of the turn does not trigger.
modifiedPrev.444.1: *Paying* a resource is the act of removing that resource from your *Rune Pool.*
modifiedPrev.444.1.a: *Pay* is an action that interacts with *Energy* and *Power.*
modifiedPrev.444.2:
When a player is instructed to *Pay* a resource, that player may remove that resource from their *Rune Pool* if it exists there. If they choose not to, the instruction is ignored.
  *Example:* When Diana, Lunari’s triggered ability resolves, if its controller has [1] Energy in their rune pool, they choose whether or not to pay that Energy as instructed. If they choose not to pay the Energy, they will not perform the additional effects of the triggered ability.
modifiedPrev.444.2.a:
If the instruction to *Pay* resources is part of paying costs for a card or ability, choosing not to pay those resources will cause the act of playing the card or ability to be undone.
  *See rule 358. Check Legality for more information.*
modifiedPrev.444.3.a: Players may only *Pay* resources when directed to by *Game Effects.*
modifiedPrev.446.1:
A *Permanent* changing its position from any space on *the Board* to another space on *the Board* is a *Move*, unless it is caused by a corrective *Recall* or an *Attached Permanent* changing locations to or with its Top-Most Card.
  *See rule 420. Move for more information.*
modifiedPrev.446.2: A card changing game zones does not in itself constitute a *Move.*
modifiedPrev.449.1: The source of the *Move* will provide details on any restrictions on legality for *Destination.*
modifiedPrev.449.2: *Units cannot Move* to a *Battlefield* that already has units from 2 other players present by any means.
modifiedPrev.458.1: Unless otherwise stated by the source of the *Recall*, Damage and statuses of a permanent will all remain unaffected by a *Recall*.
modifiedPrev.460.1: If there is an ongoing Showdown at the Battlefield where the *Combat* is staged, that *Showdown* will become a *Combat Showdown* and a *Combat* will be initiated there.
modifiedPrev.462.1:
In *Modes of Play* with more than two players, *Battlefields* with *Staged Combats* or *Combats in Progress* are *Invalid Destinations* for *Moves* of all kinds (*Standard Moves* or otherwise) by *Units* controlled by *Players* not involved in those *Combats* or who don't already have *Units* at that *Battlefield.*
  *See rule 447.2.a. for more information on Invalid Destinations.*
modifiedPrev.464.1:
*Combat* will open in one of two ways: when a *Combat* and *Showdown* are staged at the same *Battlefield* and the turn player initiates the *Showdown*; or when the turn is in a *Showdown Open State* and a *Combat* is staged at the *Battlefield* where the current *Showdown* is ongoing.
  *See rule 318. Cleanups for more information.*
modifiedPrev.464.2: *When Combat opens, it either opens with a Combat Showdown, or the current Showdown becomes a Combat Showdown.*
modifiedPrev.464.2.a: The following *Tasks* become *Outstanding*, in the order described:
modifiedPrev.464.2.b: 1. Start of combat or showdown effects happen now.
modifiedPrev.466.2:
The following *Task* becomes *Outstanding:*
  *Reminder:* Resolve any items on the chain from dealing combat damage and the Combat Cleanup and associated FEPR before performing this step.
modifiedPrev.468.1: Every instance of *Scoring* is also an instance of *Gaining* points
modifiedPrev.471.1: The player *Gains* up to one *Point*, depending on their current score.
modifiedPrev.471.1.b: When a player tries to *Gain* a *Point* through a *Conquer*, and their current *Point Total* is 1 point from the *Victory Score* of the *Mode of Play* or higher, the following occurs:
modifiedPrev.478.1.a: Applying one of the effects alters the existence of the other; or
modifiedPrev.478.1.b: Applying one of the effects alters the number of objects the other effect can influence; or
modifiedPrev.478.1.c: Applying one of the effects alters the outcome when applying the other.
modifiedPrev.479.1:
If both effects are altered by the application of the other, no *Dependency* can be established.
  *Example:* A unit with 4 [M] is under the effects of a passive ability that reads “Units you control here have their Might increased to 5 [M].” Its controller plays a spell that reads “Give a unit +2 [M], to a maximum of 5 [M].” If we apply the passive ability first, the passive ability will apply +1 [M] and the spell effect will apply +0 [M]. If we apply the spell effect first, it will apply +1 [M] while the passive ability applies +0 [M]. Both effects are altered by the sequence of applications, so we can’t establish a dependency.
modifiedPrev.479.2:
To resolve a dependency, the effects within the same layer that created the dependency must be applied such that:
  1. Identify which effect *Depends on* the other within the Layer.
  2. Apply the effect that is depended on first.
  3. Immediately apply the effect that Depends on the first effect next.
  *Example:* A unit with 4[M] is under the effects of a passive ability that reads “Units you control here have their Might increased to 5 [M].” Its controller plays Discipline on the unit. As previously established, the passive ability depends on the Discipline effect. We apply the Discipline effect first, giving the unit +2 [M], and then immediately apply the passive ability that depends on it. The unit’s final Might is 6 [M].
modifiedPrev.480.1: When an effect begins applying, it establishes a time for which it is compared against other Game Effects for purposes of resolving Layered effects as its *Timestamp.*
modifiedPrev.480.1.b: *Timestamps* are relative comparisons between effects and when they began applying to the game.
modifiedPrev.480.1.c: *Timestamps* are not referenced by Game Effects in any way. They are only used to finalize layered effects.
modifiedPrev.485.4.a: Each player provides three (3) *Battlefields*, included in their deck during deck building. Only 1 will be used, chosen during setup.
modifiedPrev.485.5: *Setup:* Each player randomly selects one (1) of their three (3) *Battlefields*. The other two are removed and will not be used for this game. The selected *Battlefields* are placed simultaneously in *the Battlefield Zone.*
modifiedPrev.485.6: *Format:* Best of 1. The first player to reach the *Victory Score* in *Points* wins the *Match.*
modifiedPrev.485.7: *First Turn Process:* The player going second channels an *extra* Rune from their Rune Deck during their first *Channel Phase* of the game.
modifiedPrev.487.4.a: Each player provides three (3) Battlefields, included in their deck during deck building. Only 1 will be used, chosen during setup.
modifiedPrev.487.5: *Setup:* Each player randomly selects one (1) of their three (3) *Battlefields*. The other two are discarded and will not be used for this game. The selected *Battlefields* are placed simultaneously between the three Players before play and will be used for this game.
modifiedPrev.487.7: *First Turn Process:* The player going first *does not draw a card* during their first *Draw Phase* of the game. The player going last channels an *extra* Rune from their Rune Deck during their first *Channel Phase* of the game.
modifiedPrev.488.4.a: Each player provides three (3) *Battlefields*, included in their deck during deck building.
modifiedPrev.488.5: *Setup:* Each player who is not going first randomly selects one (1) of their three (3) *Battlefields*. The other two are removed and will not be used for this game. The selected *Battlefields* are placed simultaneously between the players before play and will be used for this game.

modifiedPrev.805.1.a: Accelerate is functionally short for "As you play me, you may pay [1][C] as an additional cost. If you do, I enter ready."
modifiedPrev.805.2: Accelerate is an *Optional Additional Cost* to be paid as a player plays the unit with the ability.
modifiedPrev.805.2.a: Accelerate costs cannot be paid while the unit is on the board, only as part of the steps of playing a card.
modifiedPrev.805.2.b: Paying the cost generates a delayed Replacement Effect. Even if the unit loses the accelerate keyword during the finalization process, as long as the cost was paid, that unit will still enter ready.
modifiedPrev.805.3: Accelerate has no function while on the board.
modifiedPrev.805.4: Multiple instances of Accelerate are redundant.
modifiedPrev.805.5: Accelerate, and whether or not a unit has Accelerate, is a characteristic of the Unit and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
modifiedPrev.805.6: Accelerate generates a delayed replacement effect that replaces a unit entering the board exhausted with it entering ready. It does not enter exhausted and then become ready.
modifiedPrev.805.6.a: Accelerate will not interact with, or trigger, abilities that are affected by units becoming ready.

modifiedPrev.811.1.d:
Some choices made while playing a card from Hidden are restricted to the battlefield where it was hidden. A card cannot be played from Hidden if it is a spell with no valid targets under these restrictions.
  *See rule 355.6. Targeting for more information.*
modifiedPrev.811.1.d.2:
If a hidden spell or a play effect of a hidden permanent chooses any targets, those targets must be chosen from among options at that battlefield, unless the ability explicitly restricts targeting in a way that makes this impossible.
  *Example:* Blastcone Fae is a unit with Hidden and “When you play me, give a unit -2 [M] this turn, to a minimum of 1 [M].” Because this is a play effect, its target must be chosen from among units at the same battlefield if Blastcone Fae was played from Hidden.
  *Example:* Tideturner is a unit with Hidden and “When you play me, you may choose a unit you control at another location. Move me to its location and it to my original location.” Because its play effect has a targeting restriction that can never be fulfilled by a unit at its battlefield, its target may be chosen freely from among the available options.
modifiedPrev.811.1.d.3: If a hidden spell or a play effect of a hidden permanent causes you to play a unit, you must choose to play that unit at that battlefield.
